question.leadin: The Balfour Declaration supported the creation of a "national home" for members of a certain religion, which became this country.
question.text: Name this country that was invaded by five Arab nations shortly after its creation in 1948.
question.clue: This non-Persian kingdom's Book of Kings was compiled after its people's return from captivity in Babylon.

swap.leadin: Fifty-two diplomats were held hostage in an embassy in this country between 1979 and 1981.
swap.text: Name this country where that "hostage crisis" occurred after its Shah, Muhammad Reza Pahlavi, was overthrown in 1979 and replaced by a regime led by Ruhollah Khomeini.
swap.clue: The newspaper Al-Shiraa is best known for exposing covert US arms sales to this country.

question.text: This Islamic political organization was suppressed during Mubarak's time in office, but formed the Freedom and Justice Party to contest elections after Mubarak's resignation.
question.answerHtml: Muslim Brotherhood (accept The Society of the Muslim Brothers)
question.clue: Its first meeting place was created in Ismailia by its founder Hassan al-Bannah ("HAH-sen al-buh-NAH").

swap.leadin: Some Westernizing efforts in this country included educational reforms under the advisement of John Dewey and the Hat Law of 1925, which banned the use of the fez in favor of more Western-style hats.
swap.text: Name this country which had its borders redefined in the Treaty of Lausanne. Soon after, this country moved its capital to Ankara, though its most populous city is Istanbul.
swap.clue: This country contains the neolithic city of Catalhoyuk ("CHAT-ull-HOO-eck"), as well as a possible religious complex nicknamed "potbelly hill," Gobekli Tepe.

question.leadin: This polity lost land along the Mediterranean coast to the Fatimids.
question.text: Name this Muslim caliphate that succeeded the Umayyad. Its caliphs included Harun al-Rashid.
question.clue: This dynasty rose to prominence after its army defeated Marwan II at the Battle of the Zab, and it saw advancements in algebra by al-Khwarizmi and optics by Ibn al-Haytham.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Stasi intelligence agency.
swap.text: Declassified Stasi files revealed their prior knowledge of the bombing of a West Berlin discotheque by terrorists from this leader's country. This dictator later accepted responsibility for the bombing of Pan Am Flight 103 near Lockerbie, Scotland.
swap.answerHtml: Muammar Gaddafi [or Muammar Qaddafi or Muammar Muhammad Abu Minyar al-Gaddafi]
swap.clue: This leader changed his country's flag to a pure green banner and set out his ideas in the Green Book.

question.text: This dynasty replaced the Fatimids in Egypt. It was led by its namesake's Kurdish son Saladin.
question.clue: This dynasty lost territory under al-Adil and al-Kamil, and was finally driven out of its chief territory following the Battle of al-Mansurah.

swap.leadin: A dynasty ruled by this ethnic group was toppled by the led Abbasid revolution, which was led by Abu Muslim.
swap.text: Name this ethnic group that ruled the Umayyad Caliphate. The Abbasid Revolution attempted to equalize the status of muslims not of this ethnic group to muslims of this ethnic group, which Muhammad belonged to.
swap.answerHtml: Arabs [prompt on Quraysh with “What larger ethnic group are they a part of?”]
swap.clue: These people fought on both sides of the Battle of Badr and conquered the Sassanid Empire.

question.text: The Egyptian brigade was named after the Battle of Ayn Jalut, in which Sultan Qutuz, who was this type of slave soldier, defeated the invading Mongols. Thereafter, these slave-sultans ruled Egypt until 1516.
question.clue: They followed the furusiyya code, which includes cavalry tactics and horsemanship.

swap.text: The first coffeehouses were founded in this city, from which they spread rapidly throughout the Ottoman Empire and into Europe. Europeans mistakenly thought that steel with wavy patterns originated from this city.
swap.clue: A failed siege of this city led to the disintegration of a campaign spurred by the conquest of the County of Edessa, the Second Crusade.

question.text: This President of the Palestinian National Authority criticized Israel's actions. He succeeded Yasser Arafat as Chairman of the Palestinian Liberation Organization.
question.clue: One of the negotiators under Yassir Arafat at the Madrid and Oslo conferences, he has served as secretary-general of the executive committee of the PLO since 1996.

swap.text: Eden would later resign due to his failures during this incident. It consisted of an attempt to depose Gamal Nasser after he nationalized a certain waterway.
swap.clue: This conflict was the center of discussions at the Protocol of Sevres after which Charles Keightley initiated Operation Musketeer.

question.text: Fatimah, the daughter of this Sunni theologian, is also known for her dedication to women's education as part of Islamic reform. This theologian founded a namesake religious movement adopted by Muhammad bin Saud.
question.answerHtml: Muḥammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhāb [or Muḥammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhāb ibn Sulaymān al-Tamīmī; accept Wahhabi movement or Wahhabism or Wahhabiyya]
question.clue: In his hometown of Uyaynah, he gained the favor of a ruler named Uthman, whom he directed to begin a campaign of iconoclasm, destroying the domes on the gravesites of Muhammad's companion.

swap.text: This caliph sent the general Amr ibn al-'As to capture that fortress at Babylon, whereupon he founded Fustat. This caliph, who succeeded Abu Bakr and preceded Uthman, was given the title al-Farooq by Muhammad.
swap.clue: The last Sassanian king, Yazdegird III, was murdered by a brigand after his forces were defeated by this caliph's force at Qadisiyya. His creation of the qadi judgeship and divan pension system is considered the beginning of Islamic jurisprudence.

question.text: The Ghaznavids lost all its land in Persia after its defeat by this empire at the Battle of Dandanaqan. This empire expanded into Georgia under Alp Arslan.
question.clue: One ruler of it said "My punishment is heavier. I forgive you and set you free" after winning a battle.

swap.leadin: A "translation movement" of works into this language was aided by the knowledge of paper gleaned from captured Chinese prisoners after the Battle of Talas.
swap.text: Name this working language of the "House of Wisdom" in Baghdad, where Greek texts were translated for use by the Abbasid court.
swap.clue: Supposedly, books began to be mass-produced in this language after soldiers learned the secrets of printing from Chinese captives taken at the Battle of the Talas River.

question.text: This group, composed of anti-government forces, would be the target of any chemical attack by the Syrian government. It has been in a state of rebellion for over a year.
question.answerHtml: Syrian National Coalition [or National Coalition for Syrian Revolutionary and Opposition Forces, or Coalition Nationale]

swap.leadin: The organization headed by this man was responsible for the assassination of ambassador Shlomo Argov in London, leading to the 1982 invasion of Lebanon.
swap.text: Identify this namesake of a splinter group that rejected the 10 point program of the Palestine Liberation Organization. His nom de guerre translates to "father of the struggle."

question.leadin: Identify some treaties and correspondences that dealt with the Middle East after World War I FTPE.
question.text: This agreement between the British and French was one of the most controversial documents of the war. It recognized French claims to Syria and a British position in Iraq, as well as the placement of an international administration in Palestine.
question.clue: It was supplemented by the Agreement of Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne and it was modified at the Conference of San Remo.

swap.text: This golden-voiced friend of Muhammad was born into slavery as the son of Ethiopian princess captured during the Abyssinian attempt to destroy the Kaaba during the Year of the Elephant. He was later freed and became the first muezzin.
swap.answerHtml: Bilal ibn Rabah [or Bilal al-Habashi; or Bilal ibn Riyah; prompt on “ibn Rabah” or “al- Habashi” or “ibn Riyah”]
